chunks: And it is narrated from Ishaq ibn Ammar, who said:
I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: A man consulted me about hajj, and he was in a weak financial state, so I advised him not to perform hajj.
So he said: How fitting it would be for you to fall ill for a year.
He said: So I fell ill for a year.

key_terms.اسْتَشَارَنِي: He sought my advice or consultation
key_terms.الْحَجِّ: The pilgrimage to the Sacred House
key_terms.ضَعِيفَ الْحَالِ: In a weak material or financial condition

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith teach about advising someone not to go for hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith recounts that Ishaq ibn Ammar advised a financially weak man not to undertake hajj, and Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام reproved that advice. The report highlights the gravity of discouraging a person from an act of worship such as hajj and shows a consequential affliction that followed.
